nodes.statement: $(\lims,\mathsf{s},\mathsf{m})$ is conjugate to the one-sided Bernoulli $|X|$-shift.
conclusions: $(\lims,\mathsf{s},\mathsf{m})$ is conjugate to the one-sided Bernoulli $|X|$-shift.
also_stated_at:
Using a criterion from \cite{hoffman:Bernoulli} we show that the limit
dynamical system $(\lims,\mathsf{s},\mathsf{m})$ is conjugated to the one-sided Bernoulli shift.
nodes.label: theor_lims_conju_Bernoulli

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 19
nodes.statement: We will use notions and results from \cite{hoffman:Bernoulli}. First recall that a measure preserving map with entropy $\log{d}$ is called {\it uniformly $d$-to-one endomorphism} if it is almost everywhere $d$-to-one and the conditional expectation of each preimage is $1/d$. The standard example is $(X^{-\omega},\sigma,\mu_u)$, which is uniformly $|X|$-to-one. Next we want to show that $(\lims,\mathsf{s},\mathsf{m})$ is also uniformly $|X|$-to-one. By Proposition~\ref{prop_measure_prop_lims} the map $\pi:X^{-\omega}\rightarrow\lims$ is injective on the preimages $\sigma^{-1}(w)$ for almost all $w\in X^{-\omega}$, that is, $\pi$ is {\it tree adapted} in terminology of \cite{hoffman:Bernoulli}. We can apply Lemma~2.3 from \cite{hoffman:Bernoulli}, which says that a tree adapted factor of a uniform $d$-to-one endomorphism is again uniform $d$-to-one endomorphism. In particular, the shift $\mathsf{s}$ is the map of maximal entropy $\log |X|$. To prove the theorem, we use the following Theorem~5.5 in \cite{hoffman:Bernoulli}. \begin{theor} A uniform $d$-to-one endomorphism $(Y,S,\mu)$ is one-sidedly conjugated to the one-sided Bernoulli $d$-shift if and only if there exists a generating function $f$ so that $(Y,S,\mu)$ and $f$ are tree very weak Bernoulli. \end{theor} Recall the definition of tree very weak Bernoulli and generating function. Let $(Y,S,\mu)$ be uniformly $d$-to-one and $f:Y\rightarrow{R}$ be a tree adapted function to a compact metric space $R$ with metric $D$. The function $f$ is called \textit{generating} if the $\sigma$-algebra on $Y$ is generated by $S^{-i}f^{-1}(\mathcal{B}),i\geq{0}$, where $\mathcal{B}$ is the $\sigma$-algebra of Borel sets of the space $R$. Informally, ``tree very weak Bernoulli'' means that for almost all pairs of points in $Y$ their trees of preimages are close. To give a formal definition note that since $S$ is uniformly $d$-to-one, for almost all points $y\in Y$ the set $S^{-k}(y)$ contains exactly $d^k$ points, i.e. the tree of preimages is a $d$-regular rooted tree. The set $\{1,\ldots, d\}^{*}$ of finite words over $\{1,\ldots,d\}$ can be considered as a $d$-regular rooted tree, where every word $v$ is connected with $vx$ for $x\in\{1,\ldots,d\}$, and the root is the empty word $\emptyset$. We can use the tree $\{1,\ldots, d\}^{*}$ to label the trees of preimages. For almost all points $y\in Y$ there is a map $T_y:\{1,\dots,d\}^*\rightarrow{Y}$ such that $T_y(\emptyset)=y$ and $T_y(\sigma(v))=S(T_y(v))$ for all nonempty words $v\in \{1,\dots,d\}^*$. Every map $T_y$ is tree adapted, and it is uniquely defined up to an automorphism of the tree $\{1,\dots,d\}^*$. Then $(Y,S,\mu)$ and $f$ are called {\it tree very weak Bernoulli} if for any $\varepsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large $n$ there is a set $W=W(\varepsilon,n)\subset Y$ with $\mu(W)>1-\varepsilon$ such that for any $y,y'\in{W}$ \begin{equation} t_n(y,y')=\min_\psi \frac{1}{n}\sum_{v\in \{1,\dots,d\}^{*}, |v|\leq n}d^{-|v|}D(f(T_y(v)),f(T_{y'}(\psi(v))))<\varepsilon, \end{equation} where the minimum is taken over all automorphisms $\psi$ of the tree $\{1,\dots,d\}^*$. Notice that the definition of $t_n$ does not depend on the choice of $T_y$. Let us show that $(\lims,\mathsf{s},\mathsf{m})$ is tree very weak Bernoulli for the identity map $id:\lims\rightarrow\lims$. It immediately follows that $id$ is tree adapted and generating. Take a point $x\in\lims$ and let $x$ be represented by some $w\in X^{-\omega}$. Define the map $T_x:X^{*}\rightarrow\lims$ by the rule $T_x(v)=\pi(wv)$. It is enough to show that $ t_n(x,x')\rightarrow 0, n\rightarrow\infty, $ for almost all $x,x'\in\lims$. Using (\ref{eqn_diam_tile_goes_zero}) we can find $n_1$ such that $\max_{v\in X^n}\rm{diam}(\mathsf{T}_v)<\epsilon/2$ for all $n\geq n_1$. It means that $D(\pi(wv),\pi(w'v))<\epsilon/2$ for all $v,|v|\geq n_1$ (here $D$ is a fixed metric on the limit space $\lims$). Thus, taking $\psi$ to be the identical tree automorphism, we have that \[ t_n(x,x')<\frac{n_1}{n} \rm{diam}(\lims)+\frac{n-n_1}{n}\frac{\epsilon}{2}<\frac{n_1}{n} \rm{diam}(\lims)+\frac{\epsilon}{2}<\epsilon \] for $n>2n_1\rm{diam}(\lims)/\epsilon$. Hence $(\lims,\mathsf{s},\mathsf{m})$ and $id$ are tree very weak Bernoulli, which finishes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Show $\mathsf{s}$ is uniformly $|X|$-to-one (tree adapted factor of the shift), then verify Hoffman-Rudolph's tree very weak Bernoulli criterion for the identity using shrinking tile diameters.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 24
nodes.statement: The measure $\Phi_*\mu$ is a non-zero regular Borel measure on $L$. It is left to prove that it is translation invariant. Since the measure $\mu$ is $G$-invariant and the map $\Phi$ is $G$-equivariant, the measure $\Phi_*\mu$ is $G$-invariant. By the property of the map $\Phi$ we have $\phi_L(\Phi(A))=\Phi(\tau_{x_0}(A))g_0$ for every Borel set $A\subset\limGs$. Notice that since the map $\phi$ is injective, we get $\mu(A)=|X|\mu(\tau_x(A))$ (see the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop_measure lims propert}) and hence $\Phi_*\mu(B)=|X|\Phi_*\mu(\phi_L(B))$ for every Borel set $B\subset L$. It follows that the measure $\Phi_*\mu$ is $\cup_n \phi_L^n(G)$-invariant. Since $\phi_L$ is contracting, the set $\cup_n \phi_L^n(G)$ is dense in the Lie group $L$. Hence $\Phi_*\mu$ is $L$-invariant.
nodes.statement_short: $\Phi_*\mu$ is $G$-invariant and scales by $|X|$ under $\phi_L$, hence invariant under the dense set $\cup_n\phi_L^n(G)$, hence $L$-invariant.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 25
nodes.statement: The measure $\Phi_*\mu$ is the Haar measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$ by the above example. Since the Haar measure is unique up to multiplicative constant, we have that $\Phi_*\mu=c\lambda$ for some constant $c>0$ and we need to prove that $c=1$. Recall that $\mu(\mathscr{T})$ is integer by Proposition~\ref{theor_tile_measure}, and almost every point of $\limGs$ is covered by $\mu(\mathscr{T})$ tiles $\mathscr{T}\cdot g$ by Proposition~\ref{points_above}. Hence $\Phi_*\mu(T)=\Phi_*\mu(\Phi(\mathscr{T}))=\mu(\mathscr{T})$ is integer and almost every point of $\mathbb{R}^n$ is covered by $\mu(\mathscr{T})$ tiles $T+g$, $g\in\mathbb{Z}^n$, with respect to the measure $\Phi_*\mu$, and thus with respect to the Lebesgue measure $\lambda$. It follows that, if $\chi_{T+g}$ is the characteristic function of $T+g$, then $\sum_{g\in\mathbb{Z}^n}\chi_{T+g}=\mu(\mathscr{T})$ almost everywhere with respect to both measures. Hence \[ \Phi_*\mu(T)=\mu(\mathscr{T})=\int_I\sum_{g\in\mathbb{Z}^n}\chi_{T+g}d\lambda=\sum_{g\in\mathbb{Z}^n}\int_{I+g}\chi_T d\lambda=\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\chi_T d\lambda=\lambda(T), \] where $I$ is the unit cube in $\mathbb{R}^n$. Since $\mu(\mathscr{T})$ is positive, $c=1$.
nodes.statement_short: Haar uniqueness gives $\Phi_*\mu=c\lambda$; integrating the tile multiplicity over a unit cube shows $\lambda(T)=\mu(\mathscr{T})$, so $c=1$.

nodes.name: Lebesgue measure of a self-affine tile equals the measure number of the nucleus
nodes.statement: The Lebesgue measure of the self-affine tile $T$ is equal to the measure number $meas(\mathcal{N})$ of the nucleus $\mathcal{N}$ of the associated self-similar action $(\mathbb{Z}^n,X^{*})$.
conclusions: The Lebesgue measure of the self-affine tile $T$ is equal to the measure number $meas(\mathcal{N})$ of the nucleus $\mathcal{N}$ of the associated self-similar action $(\mathbb{Z}^n,X^{*})$.

nodes.name: Algorithmic computation of the nucleus and $meas(\mathcal{N})$
nodes.statement:
The nucleus of a contracting self-similar action can be found algorithmically using the program
package \cite{AutomGrp}, and the number $meas(\mathcal{N})$ can be found using the remarks after
Proposition~\ref{prop_eigenvect_transition_matr}.
conclusions: The nucleus of a contracting self-similar action can be found algorithmically using the program package \cite{AutomGrp}, and the number $meas(\mathcal{N})$ can be found using the remarks after Proposition~\ref{prop_eigenvect_transition_matr}.

nodes.name: Measures of $T\cap(T+a)$ are computable
nodes.statement:
The measures of sets $T\cap (T+a)$ for
$a\in\mathbb{Z}^n$ can be found by Remark~\ref{rem_meas_inters_tiles}.
conclusions: The measures of sets $T\cap (T+a)$ for $a\in\mathbb{Z}^n$ can be found by Remark~\ref{rem_meas_inters_tiles}.

nodes.name: Relation to the method of Gabardo and Yu
nodes.statement:
The methods developed in \cite{gab_yu:natur_til} to find the Lebesgue measure of integral
self-affine tiles are related to the discussion above. Take the complete automaton
\cite[page~11]{self_sim_groups} of the self-similar action $(\mathbb{Z}^n,X^{*})$ (it actually coincides
with the graph $B(\mathbb{Z}^n)$ from \cite{canon_numsys}), revert the direction of every edge, identify
edges with the same starting and end vertices labeled by $(d_1,d_2)$ with the same difference
$r=d_2-d_1$, and put the new label $r$ on this edge. We get the graph $\mathcal{G}(\mathbb{Z}^n)$
constructed in \cite{gab_yu:natur_til} and \cite{fract_numsys}. The set $W$ constructed using
$\mathcal{G}(\mathbb{Z}^n)$ \cite[page~195]{gab_yu:natur_til} is precisely the nucleus $\mathcal{N}$. Hence the
theory of self-similar groups provides a nice explanation to the ideas in
\cite[Section~3]{gab_yu:natur_til} and the methods developed in Sections~2,4 can be seen as its
non-abelian generalization.
nodes.statement_short: Gabardo-Yu's graph is the reversed complete automaton with difference labels and their set $W$ is the nucleus; Sections 2 and 4 generalize their method.

nodes.name: Integral self-affine tiles give lattice tilings
nodes.statement:
It is shown in \cite{lag_wang:int_self_affine_II} that integral self-affine tile $T$ gives a
lattice tiling  of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with some lattice $L\subset\mathbb{Z}^n$.
conclusions: integral self-affine tile $T$ gives a lattice tiling of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with some lattice $L\subset\mathbb{Z}^n$

nodes.name: Does the tile of a contracting self-similar action give a tiling?
nodes.statement:
An interesting open question is
whether this holds for any (self-replicating) contracting self-similar action $(G,X^{*})$ (or at
least for self-similar actions of torsion-free nilpotent groups), i.e. the tile $\mathscr{T}$ gives a
tiling of $\limGs$ with some subgroup $H< G$.

nodes.name: Freire-Lopes-Mane invariant measure
nodes.statement:
Let
$f(z)\in\mathbb{C}(z)$ be a rational map of the Riemann sphere $\hat{\mathbb{C}}$ of degree $d\geq 2$. It is
proved in \cite{invmeas_rat} that there exists a natural $f$-invariant probability measure $\mu_f$
with the support on the Julia set $J(f)$.
assumptions: Let $f(z)\in\mathbb{C}(z)$ be a rational map of the Riemann sphere $\hat{\mathbb{C}}$ of degree $d\geq 2$.
conclusions: there exists a natural $f$-invariant probability measure $\mu_f$ with the support on the Julia set $J(f)$

nodes.name: Rational maps are Bernoulli (Heicklen-Hoffman)
nodes.statement:
In \cite{rational_bernoulli}, D.~Heicklen and C.~Hoffman
showed that the dynamical system $(J(f),f,\mu_f)$ is conjugated to the one-sided Bernoulli
$d$-shift, proving the conjecture in \cite{invmeas_rat,lub:entr_ration}.
conclusions: the dynamical system $(J(f),f,\mu_f)$ is conjugated to the one-sided Bernoulli $d$-shift

nodes.name: Bernoulli property for sub-hyperbolic rational maps via iterated monodromy groups
nodes.statement:
In the case of
sub-hyperbolic rational functions this result also follows from
Theorem~\ref{theor_lims_conju_Bernoulli} using the theory of iterated monodromy groups developed in
\cite{self_sim_groups}.
assumptions: In the case of sub-hyperbolic rational functions
conclusions: this result also follows from Theorem~\ref{theor_lims_conju_Bernoulli}

nodes.name: Argument via iterated monodromy groups
nodes.statement:
Let $f$ be a sub-hyperbolic rational function and let $\mathcal{M}=\hat{\mathbb{C}}\setminus\overline{P}_f$, where $P_f$
is the post-critical set of $f$. Then $f$ defines a $d$-fold partial self-covering $f:
f^{-1}(\mathcal{M})\rightarrow\mathcal{M}$. Take a base point $t\in\mathcal{M}$ and let $T_t$ be the tree of preimages
$f^{-n}(t)$, $n\geq 0$, where every vertex $z\in f^{-n}(t)$ is connected by an edge to $f(z)\in
f^{-n+1}(t)$. The fundamental group $\pi_1(\mathcal{M},t)$ acts by automorphisms on $T_t$ through the
monodromy action on every level $f^{-n}(t)$. The quotient of $\pi_1(\mathcal{M},t)$ by the kernel of its
action on $T_t$ is the \textit{iterated monodromy group} $IMG(f)$ of the map $f$. The group
$IMG(f)$ is contracting self-similar group and the limit dynamical system $(\lims[IMG(f)],\mathsf{s})$ is
conjugated to $(J(f),f)$ by Theorem~6.4.4 in \cite{self_sim_groups}. Under this conjugation the
measure $\mathsf{m}$ is send to the measure $\mu_f$, and we can apply
Theorem~\ref{theor_lims_conju_Bernoulli} to the dynamical system $(J(f),f,\mu_f)$.
nodes.statement_short: Identify $(J(f),f)$ with the limit dynamical system of $IMG(f)$ (Nekrashevych Thm 6.4.4), carrying $\mathsf{m}$ to $\mu_f$, and apply Theorem 19.

nodes.name: Introduce $w$ and its suffixes $w_n$
nodes.statement:
Let $w=\ldots x_2x_1\in X^{-\omega}$ and denote $w_n=x_n\ldots x_2x_1$ for $n\geq 1$. Observe, that
$V(w)\subseteq V(w_n)$ and $V(w_n)\subseteq V(w_m)$ for $n\geq m$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce $w$ and its suffixes $w_n$; $V(w_n)$ decreases.

nodes.name: Inverse limit of finite path sets gives a left-infinite path
nodes.statement:
Take a vertex $v\in \cap_{n\geq 1} V(w_n)$. Let $P_n$ be the set of all paths $e_n\ldots e_2e_1$
labeled by $w_n$ and ending in $v$. The set $P_n$ is a finite non-empty set for every $n$, and
$e_{n-1}\ldots e_2e_1\in P_{n-1}$ for every path $e_n\ldots e_2e_1\in P_n$. Since the inverse limit
of a sequence of finite non-empty sets is non-empty, there exists a left-infinite path $\ldots
e_2e_1$ labeled by $w$ and ending in $v$.
nodes.statement_short: Inverse limit of finite path sets gives a left-infinite path ending at $v$.

nodes.name: Hence $V(w)=\cap_n V(w_n)$, proving the second equality.
nodes.statement:
Then $v\in V(w)$ and we get
\begin{equation} V(w)=\bigcap_{n\geq 1} V(w_n).
\end{equation}
From this follows that $|V(w)|=\min\limits_{n\geq 1} |V(w_n)|$ for $w\in X^{-\omega}$. Then
\[
\min_{w\in X^{-\omega}} |V(w)|=\min_{w\in X^{-\omega}} \min_{n\geq 1} |V(w_n)|=\min_{w\in X^*} |V(w)|
\]
and the second equality of the theorem is proved.
nodes.statement_short: Hence $V(w)=\cap_n V(w_n)$, proving the second equality.

nodes.name: Define the minimum $k$ and the sets $\mathcal{O}$, $\mathcal
nodes.statement:
Define the integer $k=\min_{w\in X^{-\omega}} |V(w)|$ and consider the set
$\mathcal{O}=\mathcal{O}(\Gamma)\subseteq X^{-\omega}$ of all sequences $w\in X^{-\omega}$ such that $|V(w)|=k$.
Define $\mathcal{O}^*$ as the set of finite words that satisfy the same condition. We have the
following lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Define the minimum $k$ and the sets $\mathcal{O}$, $\mathcal{O}^*$.

nodes.name: Lemma 1 and its proof.
nodes.statement:
\begin{lemma} The set $\mathcal{O}$ is open and dense in $X^{-\omega}$, and $\mu_p(\mathcal{O})=1$. For each
$w\in\mathcal{O}$ there is a beginning of $w$ that belongs to $\mathcal{O}^*$. Equivalently,
$\mathcal{O}=\cup_{w\in\mathcal{O}^*}X^{-\omega} w$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
If $w\in\mathcal{O}$ then $k=|V(w)|=\min_{n\geq 1} |V(w_n)|$ and there exists $N\geq 1$ such that
$|V(w_N)|=k$. Then $k\leq |V(\omega w_N)|\leq |V(w_N)|=k$ for all $\omega\in X^{-\omega}$. Hence
$w_N\in\mathcal{O}^*$, $X^{-\omega} w_N\subseteq\mathcal{O}$ and so $\mathcal{O}$ is open, and thus
measurable.

Let $u\in X^*$ be such that $|V(u)|=k$. Let us show that if $w\in X^{-\omega}$ contains the subword $u$
then $w\in\mathcal{O}$. If $w=w'u$ then $k\leq |V(w'u)|\leq |V(u)|=k$ and $w\in\mathcal{O}$.
Observe that $V(ux)$ is the set of those vertices $v\in V$ for which there exists an edge labeled
by $x$ which starts in some vertex of $V(u)$ and ends in $v$. Since the graph $\Gamma$ is
right-resolving there is no more than one such an edge for each vertex of $V(u)$, and thus
$|V(ux)|\leq |V(u)|$. It implies that if $w=w'uu'$ than $k\leq |V(w)|\leq |V(u)|=k$ and thus
$|V(w)|=k$, so $w\in\mathcal{O}$. The Bernoulli measure of the set of all words $w'uu', u'\in X^*,
w'\in X^{-\omega}$, is equal to $1$. Thus $\mu_p(\mathcal{O})=1$. It follows also that $\mathcal{O}$ is
dense in $X^{-\omega}$.
\end{proof}
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 1 and its proof.

nodes.name: Count vertices a.e. equal to $k$ and integrate.
nodes.statement:
By construction of the set $\mathcal{O}$ for every $w\in\mathcal{O}$ there exist exactly $k$
vertices $v$ such that $w\in F_v$. Let $\chi_{F_v}$ be the characteristic function of the set
$F_v$. Then $\sum_{v\in V}\chi_{F_v}=k$ almost everywhere. Integrating we get
$\mu_p(\Gamma)=\sum\limits_{v\in V} \mu_p(F_v)=k$.
nodes.statement_short: Count vertices a.e. equal to $k$ and integrate.

nodes.name: A minimizing prefix forces minimality
nodes.statement:
If $w\in\mathcal{O}$ then $k=|V(w)|=\min_{n\geq 1} |V(w_n)|$ and there exists $N\geq 1$ such that
$|V(w_N)|=k$. Then $k\leq |V(\omega w_N)|\leq |V(w_N)|=k$ for all $\omega\in X^{-\omega}$. Hence
$w_N\in\mathcal{O}^*$, $X^{-\omega} w_N\subseteq\mathcal{O}$ and so $\mathcal{O}$ is open, and thus
measurable.
nodes.statement_short: A minimizing prefix forces minimality; hence $\mathcal{O}$ is open.

nodes.name: Claim: any sequence containing a minimizing word $u$ lies in
nodes.statement:
Let $u\in X^*$ be such that $|V(u)|=k$. Let us show that if $w\in X^{-\omega}$ contains the subword $u$
then $w\in\mathcal{O}$. If $w=w'u$ then $k\leq |V(w'u)|\leq |V(u)|=k$ and $w\in\mathcal{O}$.
Observe that $V(ux)$ is the set of those vertices $v\in V$ for which there exists an edge labeled
by $x$ which starts in some vertex of $V(u)$ and ends in $v$. Since the graph $\Gamma$ is
right-resolving there is no more than one such an edge for each vertex of $V(u)$, and thus
$|V(ux)|\leq |V(u)|$. It implies that if $w=w'uu'$ than $k\leq |V(w)|\leq |V(u)|=k$ and thus
$|V(w)|=k$, so $w\in\mathcal{O}$.
nodes.statement_short: Claim: any sequence containing a minimizing word $u$ lies in $\mathcal{O}$.

nodes.statement: If $w=w'u$ then $k\leq |V(w'u)|\leq |V(u)|=k$ and $w\in\mathcal{O}$.
nodes.statement_short: Case $w=w'u$.

nodes.name: Right-resolving gives $|V(ux)|\le|V(u)|$.
nodes.statement:
Observe that $V(ux)$ is the set of those vertices $v\in V$ for which there exists an edge labeled
by $x$ which starts in some vertex of $V(u)$ and ends in $v$. Since the graph $\Gamma$ is
right-resolving there is no more than one such an edge for each vertex of $V(u)$, and thus
$|V(ux)|\leq |V(u)|$.
nodes.statement_short: Right-resolving gives $|V(ux)|\le|V(u)|$.

nodes.name: Hence $w=w'uu'$ lies in $\mathcal{O}$.
nodes.statement:
It implies that if $w=w'uu'$ than $k\leq |V(w)|\leq |V(u)|=k$ and thus
$|V(w)|=k$, so $w\in\mathcal{O}$.
nodes.statement_short: Hence $w=w'uu'$ lies in $\mathcal{O}$.

nodes.name: Almost every sequence contains $u$: full measure and density
nodes.statement:
The Bernoulli measure of the set of all words $w'uu', u'\in X^*,
w'\in X^{-\omega}$, is equal to $1$. Thus $\mu_p(\mathcal{O})=1$. It follows also that $\mathcal{O}$ is
dense in $X^{-\omega}$.
nodes.statement_short: Almost every sequence contains $u$: full measure and density.

nodes.name: Disjoint decomposition of $B_v$ gives the right eigen-equati
nodes.statement:
By construction, for every vertex $v\in V$ we have
\[
B_v=\bigsqcup_{v\stackrel{x}\rightarrow u} xB_u
\]
(here the union is disjoint because the graph $\Gamma$ is right-resolving). It implies
\[
\mu_p(B_v)=\sum_{v\stackrel{x}\rightarrow u} p_x\mu_p(B_{u})=\sum_{u\in V} t_{vu}\mu_p(B_{u}).
\]
Thus the nonzero vector $\vec \mu_p(\mathscr{B})$ is the right eigenvector of $T_p$ for the eigenvalue~$1$.
nodes.statement_short: Disjoint decomposition of $B_v$ gives the right eigen-equation.

nodes.name: Decomposition of $F_v$ gives $\vec\mu_p(\mathscr{F})\le\vec\
nodes.statement_short: Decomposition of $F_v$ gives $\vec\mu_p(\mathscr{F})\le\vec\mu_p(\mathscr{F})T_p$.

nodes.name: Nonnegative matrix theory finishes.
nodes.statement:
The standard arguments based on the theory of nonnegative matrices (see for example \cite[proof of
Theorem 4.5]{he_hui:self_affine}, \cite[p. 197]{gab_yu:natur_til}, \cite{handbook:rothblum}) end
the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Nonnegative matrix theory finishes.

nodes.name: Claim: $\mu(A)\ge|X|\mu(\tau_x(A))$.
nodes.statement:
Let us show that $\mu(A)\geq |X|\mu(\tau_x(A))$ for any Borel set $A$. Consider sequences which
represent points of the sets $A$ and $\tau_x(A)$:
\[
\pi^{-1}_{\limGs[]}(A)=\bigcup_{g\in G}T_g\cdot g \ \ \Rightarrow \ \
\pi^{-1}_{\limGs[]}(\tau_x(A))=\bigcup_{g\in G}T_g g(x)\cdot g|_x.
\]








It implies
\[
\mu(\tau_x(A))\leq \sum_{g\in G} \frac{1}{|X|}\mu_u (T_g)=\frac{1}{|X|}\mu(A).
\]
nodes.statement_short: Claim: $\mu(A)\ge|X|\mu(\tau_x(A))$.

nodes.name: Describe the preimages of $A$ and $\tau_x(A)$.
nodes.statement:
Consider sequences which
represent points of the sets $A$ and $\tau_x(A)$:
\[
\pi^{-1}_{\limGs[]}(A)=\bigcup_{g\in G}T_g\cdot g \ \ \Rightarrow \ \
\pi^{-1}_{\limGs[]}(\tau_x(A))=\bigcup_{g\in G}T_g g(x)\cdot g|_x.
\]
nodes.statement_short: Describe the preimages of $A$ and $\tau_x(A)$.

nodes.name: Sum to get the inequality.
nodes.statement:
It implies
\[
\mu(\tau_x(A))\leq \sum_{g\in G} \frac{1}{|X|}\mu_u (T_g)=\frac{1}{|X|}\mu(A).
\]
nodes.statement_short: Sum to get the inequality.

nodes.name: Iterate $n$ times and compare with the cover of $\mathscr{T}
nodes.statement:
By applying this inequality $n$ times we get
$|X|^n\mu(\mathscr{T}_v)=|X|^n\mu(\tau_v(\mathscr{T}))\leq\mu(\mathscr{T})$ for $v\in{X}^n$. Since $\mathscr{T}=\cup_{u\in
X^n}\mathscr{T}_{u}$ we have that
\[
\mu(\mathscr{T})\leq\sum_{u\in X^n}\mu(\mathscr{T}_{u})\leq\sum_{u\in X^n}\frac{1}{|X|^n}\mu(\mathscr{T})=\mu(\mathscr{T}).
\]
nodes.statement_short: Iterate $n$ times and compare with the cover of $\mathscr{T}$ by level-$n$ tiles.

nodes.name: Equalities hold: items 1 and 2.
nodes.statement:
Hence all the above inequalities are actually equalities, $\mu(\mathscr{T})=|X|^n\mu(\mathscr{T}_{u})$ for
every $u\in X^n$, and $\mu(\mathscr{T}_u\cap\mathscr{T}_{u'})=0$ for different $u,u'\in X^n$.
nodes.statement_short: Equalities hold: items 1 and 2.

nodes.name: Small $\mu(\tau_x(A))$ gives small $\mu(A)$.
nodes.statement:
Notice that since every Borel set $A\subset\mathscr{T}$ can be approximated by unions of tiles of the
same level 
and using items 1 and 2 we have that if $\mu(\tau_x(A))<\varepsilon$ then $\mu(A)<\varepsilon|X|$.
nodes.statement_short: Small $\mu(\tau_x(A))$ gives small $\mu(A)$.

nodes.name: It remains to prove item 3.
nodes.statement: It is left to prove item 3.
nodes.statement_short: It remains to prove item 3.

nodes.name: Claim: item 3 holds for tiles $\mathscr{T}_v$.
nodes.statement:
First, let us show that the assertion holds for the tiles $\mathscr{T}_v$.
Since the measure $\mu|_{\mathscr{T}}$ is concentrated on the tile $\mathscr{T}$, up to sets of measure zero
the set $\tau_x^{-1}(\mathscr{T}_v)$ is equal $\mathscr{T}_u$ if $v=ux$, and is empty if the last letter of $v$
is not $x$. Really, if $t\in\tau_x^{-1}(\mathscr{T}_{ux})$ and $t\in\mathscr{T}_v$ with $v\neq u, |v|=|u|$,
then $\tau_x(t)\in\mathscr{T}_{vx}\cap\mathscr{T}_{ux}$ and the measure of such points is zero. Hence
\[
\mu|_{\mathscr{T}}(\mathscr{T}_v)=\frac{1}{|X|}\mu|_{\mathscr{T}}(\mathscr{T}_u)=\sum_{x\in X}
\frac{1}{|X|}\mu|_{\mathscr{T}}(\tau_x^{-1}(\mathscr{T}_v)).
\]
nodes.statement_short: Claim: item 3 holds for tiles $\mathscr{T}_v$.

nodes.name: Up to null sets, $\tau_x^{-1}(\mathscr{T}_v)$ is $\mathscr{T
nodes.statement:
Since the measure $\mu|_{\mathscr{T}}$ is concentrated on the tile $\mathscr{T}$, up to sets of measure zero
the set $\tau_x^{-1}(\mathscr{T}_v)$ is equal $\mathscr{T}_u$ if $v=ux$, and is empty if the last letter of $v$
is not $x$.
nodes.statement_short: Up to null sets, $\tau_x^{-1}(\mathscr{T}_v)$ is $\mathscr{T}_u$ or empty.

nodes.name: Overlaps have measure zero.
nodes.statement:
Really, if $t\in\tau_x^{-1}(\mathscr{T}_{ux})$ and $t\in\mathscr{T}_v$ with $v\neq u, |v|=|u|$,
then $\tau_x(t)\in\mathscr{T}_{vx}\cap\mathscr{T}_{ux}$ and the measure of such points is zero.
nodes.statement_short: Overlaps have measure zero.

nodes.name: Hence the self-similarity identity on tiles.
nodes.statement:
Hence
\[
\mu|_{\mathscr{T}}(\mathscr{T}_v)=\frac{1}{|X|}\mu|_{\mathscr{T}}(\mathscr{T}_u)=\sum_{x\in X}
\frac{1}{|X|}\mu|_{\mathscr{T}}(\tau_x^{-1}(\mathscr{T}_v)).
\]
nodes.statement_short: Hence the self-similarity identity on tiles.

nodes.name: Approximate Borel sets by tiles.
nodes.statement: Now we can approximate any Borel set by unions of tiles and pass to the limit.
nodes.statement_short: Approximate Borel sets by tiles.

nodes.name: Preimage of the tile via nucleus sets
nodes.statement:
By Proposition~\ref{prop_asympt_Moore_diagr} we have
\[
\pi^{-1}_{\limGs[]}(\mathscr{T})=\bigcup_{g\in\mathcal{N}}F_g\cdot g^{-1},
\]
where the sets $F_g$ are defined using the graph $\Gamma_{\mathcal{N}}$ (see Section~2). Thus
\[
\mu(\mathscr{T})=\sum_{g\in\mathcal{N}}\mu_u(F_g)=meas(\mathcal{N}),
\]
which is integer by Theorem~\ref{theor_measure_graph_integer}.
nodes.statement_short: Preimage of the tile via nucleus sets; measure is $meas(\mathcal{N})$, integer by Theorem 1.

nodes.name: $\mu(\mathscr{T})\ge1$ since $F_1$ is everything.
nodes.statement:
Observe that $\mu(\mathscr{T})\geq 1$
because $F_g=X^{-\omega}$ for $g=1\in\mathcal{N}$.
nodes.statement_short: $\mu(\mathscr{T})\ge1$ since $F_1$ is everything.

nodes.name: Under OSC, the measure is 1 by Corollary 4.
nodes.statement:
If the action satisfies the open set condition then $\mu(\mathscr{T})=meas(\Gamma_{\mathcal{N}})=1$ by
Corollary~\ref{cor_meas_sum_meas}.
nodes.statement_short: Under OSC, the measure is 1 by Corollary 4.

nodes.name: Without OSC, a restriction-closed set of nontrivial elements
nodes.statement:
Suppose now that the action does not satisfy the open set condition. Then there exists an element
$h$ of the nucleus, whose all restrictions are non-trivial. Let $\mathcal{N}_1$ be the set of all
restrictions of $h$, and $\Gamma_{\mathcal{N}_1}$ be the corresponding graph. Then by Proposition~\ref{prop cup B_v eq cup F_v}
\[
\sum_{g\in\mathcal{N}_1}\mu_u(F_g)=meas(\Gamma_{\mathcal{N}_1})\geq 1.
\]
Thus $\mu(\mathscr{T})=\sum_{g\in\mathcal{N}}\mu_u(F_g)\geq meas(\Gamma_{\mathcal{N}_1})+\mu_u(F_{g=1})\geq 2$.
nodes.statement_short: Without OSC, a restriction-closed set of nontrivial elements contributes at least 1 more.

nodes.name: Define multiplicity $n_x$.
nodes.statement:
For each $x\in\limGs$ we define the number $n_x$ of such $g\in G$ that the tile $\mathscr{T}\cdot g$
contains $x$.
nodes.statement_short: Define multiplicity $n_x$.

nodes.name: Claim: $n_x\ge meas(\Gamma_{\mathcal{N}})$.
nodes.statement:
First we prove the inequality. Let $x\in\limGs$ be represented by the pair $w\cdot g$ from
$X^{-\omega}\times G$. Then $|V(w)|\geq meas(\Gamma_{\mathcal{N}})$ by Theorem~\ref{theor_measure_graph_integer}. If
$h\in V(w)$ it means that the sequence $w$ ends in $h$, which by
Proposition~\ref{prop_asympt_Moore_diagr} means that there is a sequence $u_h\in X^{-\omega}$ such that $w$
is asymptotically equivalent to $u_h\cdot h$. It follows that $w\cdot g$ is asymptotically
equivalent to $u_h\cdot hg$. It means, in turn, that $x$ belongs to the tile $\mathscr{T}\cdot hg$ for
every $h\in V(w)$. It follows that $n_x\geq meas(\Gamma_{\mathcal{N}})$.
nodes.statement_short: Claim: $n_x\ge meas(\Gamma_{\mathcal{N}})$.

nodes.name: Represent $x$ by $w\cdot g$
nodes.statement:
Let $x\in\limGs$ be represented by the pair $w\cdot g$ from
$X^{-\omega}\times G$. Then $|V(w)|\geq meas(\Gamma_{\mathcal{N}})$ by Theorem~\ref{theor_measure_graph_integer}.
nodes.statement_short: Represent $x$ by $w\cdot g$; $|V(w)|\ge meas$ by Theorem 1.

If
$h\in V(w)$ it means that the sequence $w$ ends in $h$, which by
Proposition~\ref{prop_asympt_Moore_diagr} means that there is a sequence $u_h\in X^{-\omega}$ such that $w$
is asymptotically equivalent to $u_h\cdot h$.
nodes.statement_short: Each $h\in V(w)$ gives an equivalent representative $u_h\cdot h$.

nodes.statement:
It follows that $w\cdot g$ is asymptotically

every $h\in V(w)$. It follows that $n_x\geq meas(\Gamma_{\mathcal{N}})$.
nodes.statement_short: So $x$ lies in $\mathscr{T}\cdot hg$ for each such $h$.

nodes.statement:
By the same considerations as above we see that if
$w\cdot g$ represents a point $x$ with $n_x=meas(\Gamma_{\mathcal{N}})$ then $|V(w)|=meas(\Gamma_{\mathcal{N}})$, that
is, $w$ belongs to $\mathcal{O}$. In other words, the set $\mathcal{O}\times G$ is closed under the
asymptotic equivalence relation on $X^{-\omega}\times G$, and it is the inverse image of the set
$\dot{\limGs}$ under the factor map $\pi_{\limGs[]}$.
nodes.statement_short: Exact-multiplicity points lift exactly to $\mathcal{O}\times G$.

nodes.name: Openness and density transfer by Lemma 1.
nodes.statement:
Since the set $\mathcal{O}\times G$ is open
and dense in $X^{-\omega}\times G$ by Lemma~\ref{lemma_set V open dense}, the same hold for $\dot{\limGs}$
in $\limGs$.
nodes.statement_short: Openness and density transfer by Lemma 1.

nodes.name: Complement is null by Lemma 1.
nodes.statement:
The complement of $\dot{\limGs}$ has measure $0$, because the complement of the set
$\mathcal{O}$ has measure $0$ by Lemma~\ref{lemma_set V open dense}.
nodes.statement_short: Complement is null by Lemma 1.

nodes.name: Take a boundary point of exact multiplicity $k$.
nodes.statement: Take $x\in\partial\mathscr{T}$. Suppose that $x$ is covered by exactly $k=\mu(\mathscr{T})$ tiles.
nodes.statement_short: Take a boundary point of exact multiplicity $k$.

nodes.name: Choose a neighbourhood meeting only the $k$ tiles through $x
nodes.statement:
Let
$U\subset\dot{\limGs}$ be the neighborhood of $x$ which intersects with finitely many tiles, say
with $l\geq k$ tiles. By subtracting any tile that does not contain $x$ we may suppose that $l=k$,
that is, $U$ has nonempty intersection only with those tiles that contain $x$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose a neighbourhood meeting only the $k$ tiles through $x$.

nodes.name: A nearby point outside $\mathscr{T}$ has multiplicity $<k$:
nodes.statement:
Now, since $x$ is in
the boundary of $\mathscr{T}$, there is a point $x'$ in $U$ that is not covered by $\mathscr{T}$ (otherwise
$x\in U\subset\mathscr{T}$), thus $x'$ is covered by less than $k$ tiles, contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: A nearby point outside $\mathscr{T}$ has multiplicity $<k$: contradiction.

nodes.name: So $\partial\mathscr{T}$ is null.
nodes.statement:
Hence
$\partial\mathscr{T}$ is in the complement of $\dot{\limGs}$ and has measure $0$.
nodes.statement_short: So $\partial\mathscr{T}$ is null.

nodes.name: Tile measure equals $k=\min|V(w)|$ by Theorems 11 and 1.
nodes.statement_short: Tile measure equals $k=\min|V(w)|$ by Theorems 11 and 1.

nodes.name: Write the preimage of $\alpha(\mathscr{T})$ as $\cup T_g\cdo
nodes.statement:
Consider
\[
\pi_Y^{-1}(\alpha(\mathscr{T}))=\bigcup_{g\in G} T_g\cdot g\quad (\mbox{here } T_g\subseteq Y^{-\omega}),
\]
where $\pi_Y:Y^{-\omega}\times G\rightarrow \limGs$ is the canonical projection.
nodes.statement_short: Write the preimage of $\alpha(\mathscr{T})$ as $\cup T_g\cdot g$.

nodes.name: Claim: every $w$ lies in at least $k$ sets $T_g$.
nodes.statement:
Take $w\in Y^{-\omega}$ and let us prove that there exist at least $k$ elements $g\in G$ such that
$w\in T_g$. The tiles $\mathscr{T}\cdot g$ cover the limit $G$-space $\limGs[(G,X^*)]$, and we can find
$g\in G$ such that if $x=\alpha^{-1}(y)$ for $y=\pi_{Y}(w\cdot g)\in\limGs[(G,Y^*)]$ then $x$
belongs to the tile $\mathscr{T}$. Then $x$ is represented by the sequence $u\cdot 1$ for $u\in X^{-\omega}$.
Equation~(\ref{eqn_theor_meraXY_mu tile }) implies $|V(u)|\geq k$ and so there exist $k$ elements
$h_1,\ldots, h_k\in\mathcal{N}$ and sequences $u_1,\ldots,u_k\in X^{-\omega}$ such that for every $i$ there
exists a left-infinite path in the nucleus $\mathcal{N}$ which ends in $h_i$ and is labeled by $(u,u_i)$.
By Proposition~\ref{prop_asympt_Moore_diagr}
\[
x=\pi_X(u\cdot 1)=\pi_X(u_i\cdot h_i)\quad\mbox{ and }\quad x\cdot h_i^{-1}\in\mathscr{T}
\]
for every $i=1,\ldots, k$. Then
\[
\pi_Y(w\cdot gh_i^{-1})=\pi_Y(w\cdot g)h_i^{-1}=y\cdot h_i^{-1}=\alpha(x\cdot
h_i^{-1})\in\alpha(\mathscr{T})
\]
and thus $w\in T_{gh_i^{-1}}$ for all $i=1,\ldots, k$.
nodes.statement_short: Claim: every $w$ lies in at least $k$ sets $T_g$.

nodes.name: Choose $g$ so that $x=\alpha^{-1}(y)$ lies in $\mathscr{T}$,
nodes.statement:
The tiles $\mathscr{T}\cdot g$ cover the limit $G$-space $\limGs[(G,X^*)]$, and we can find
$g\in G$ such that if $x=\alpha^{-1}(y)$ for $y=\pi_{Y}(w\cdot g)\in\limGs[(G,Y^*)]$ then $x$
belongs to the tile $\mathscr{T}$. Then $x$ is represented by the sequence $u\cdot 1$ for $u\in X^{-\omega}$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose $g$ so that $x=\alpha^{-1}(y)$ lies in $\mathscr{T}$, represented by $u\cdot 1$.

nodes.name: $|V(u)|\ge k$ gives $k$ nucleus paths.
nodes.statement:
Equation~(\ref{eqn_theor_meraXY_mu tile }) implies $|V(u)|\geq k$ and so there exist $k$ elements
$h_1,\ldots, h_k\in\mathcal{N}$ and sequences $u_1,\ldots,u_k\in X^{-\omega}$ such that for every $i$ there
exists a left-infinite path in the nucleus $\mathcal{N}$ which ends in $h_i$ and is labeled by $(u,u_i)$.
nodes.statement_short: $|V(u)|\ge k$ gives $k$ nucleus paths.

nodes.name: Proposition 8 gives $x\cdot h_i^{-1}\in\mathscr{T}$.
nodes.statement_short: Proposition 8 gives $x\cdot h_i^{-1}\in\mathscr{T}$.

nodes.name: Hence $w\in T_{gh_i^{-1}}$ for all $i$.
nodes.statement:
Then
\[
\pi_Y(w\cdot gh_i^{-1})=\pi_Y(w\cdot g)h_i^{-1}=y\cdot h_i^{-1}=\alpha(x\cdot
h_i^{-1})\in\alpha(\mathscr{T})
\]
and thus $w\in T_{gh_i^{-1}}$ for all $i=1,\ldots, k$.
nodes.statement_short: Hence $w\in T_{gh_i^{-1}}$ for all $i$.

nodes.name: Integrate: $\mu_Y(\alpha(\mathscr{T}))\ge\mu_X(\mathscr{T})$
nodes.statement:
Let $\chi_{T_g}$ be the characteristic function of the set $T_g$. Then $\sum_{g\in
G}\chi_{T_g}(x)\geq k$ for almost all $x$. Integrating we get
$\mu_{(G,Y^*)}(\alpha(\mathscr{T}))=\sum_{g\in G} \mu_u(T_g)\geq k=\mu_{(G,X^*)}(\mathscr{T})$.
nodes.statement_short: Integrate: $\mu_Y(\alpha(\mathscr{T}))\ge\mu_X(\mathscr{T})$.

nodes.name: Claim: $\mu_Y(\alpha(\mathscr{T}_v))\le\mu_X(\mathscr{T}_v)$
nodes.statement:
Let us now show that $\mu_{(G,Y^*)}(\alpha(\mathscr{T}_v))\leq\mu_{(G,X^*)}(\mathscr{T}_v)$ for any $v\in X^*$.
Indeed, let $n=|v|$, then it follows from Theorem \ref{theor_limsX hom limsY} that
$\alpha(\mathscr{T}_v)=\alpha(\tau_v(\mathscr{T}))=\tau_u(\alpha(\mathscr{T}))g$ for some word $u\in Y^n$ and $g\in
G$. Thus
\begin{eqnarray*}
\mu_{(G,Y^*)}(\alpha(\mathscr{T}_v))&=&\mu_{(G,Y^*)}(\tau_u(\alpha(\mathscr{T})))\leq\frac{1}{|X|^n}\mu_{(G,Y^*)}(\alpha(\mathscr{T}))=\\
&=&\frac{1}{|X|^n}\mu_{(G,X^*)}(\mathscr{T})=\mu_{(G,X^*)}(\mathscr{T}_v).
\end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Claim: $\mu_Y(\alpha(\mathscr{T}_v))\le\mu_X(\mathscr{T}_v)$.

nodes.name: Theorem 9 maps $\mathscr{T}_v$ to a translate of $\tau_u(\al
nodes.statement:
Indeed, let $n=|v|$, then it follows from Theorem \ref{theor_limsX hom limsY} that
$\alpha(\mathscr{T}_v)=\alpha(\tau_v(\mathscr{T}))=\tau_u(\alpha(\mathscr{T}))g$ for some word $u\in Y^n$ and $g\in
G$.
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 9 maps $\mathscr{T}_v$ to a translate of $\tau_u(\alpha(\mathscr{T}))$.

nodes.name: Chain of inequalities.
nodes.statement_short: Chain of inequalities.

nodes.name: Claim: $\mu_Y\circ\alpha$ is absolutely continuous w.r.t. $\
nodes.statement:
Let us prove that $\mu_{(G,Y^*)}\circ\alpha$ is absolutely continuous with respect to
$\mu_{(G,X^*)}$. Indeed, let $\mu_{(G,X^*)}(A)<\varepsilon$, $\pi^{-1}_{X}(A)=\cup_g T_g\cdot g$.
Then $\sum_g\mu_u(T_g)<\varepsilon$. It follows that there exist $v_{i,g}\in X^*$ such that
$T_g\subset\cup_iX^{-\omega} v_{i,g}$ and $\sum_{i,g}|X|^{-|v_{i,g}|}<\varepsilon$. Then
$A\subset\cup_{i,g}\mathscr{T}_{v_{i,g}}\cdot g$, and we have that
$\sum_{i,g}\mu_{(G,X^*)}(\mathscr{T}_{v_{i,g}})<\varepsilon\mu_{(G,X^*)}(\mathscr{T})$. Then
$\mu_{(G,Y^*)}(\alpha(A))\leq\sum\mu_{(G,Y^*)}(\alpha(\mathscr{T}_{v_{i,g}}))\leq\sum\mu_{(G,X^*)}(\mathscr{T}_{v_{i,g}})<\varepsilon\mu_{(G,X^*)}(\mathscr{T})$.
Since $\varepsilon$ is arbitrary, we are done.
nodes.statement_short: Claim: $\mu_Y\circ\alpha$ is absolutely continuous w.r.t. $\mu_X$.

nodes.name: Take $A$ of small measure.
nodes.statement:
Indeed, let $\mu_{(G,X^*)}(A)<\varepsilon$, $\pi^{-1}_{X}(A)=\cup_g T_g\cdot g$.
Then $\sum_g\mu_u(T_g)<\varepsilon$.
nodes.statement_short: Take $A$ of small measure.

nodes.name: Cover by cylinders and hence by small tiles.
nodes.statement:
It follows that there exist $v_{i,g}\in X^*$ such that
$T_g\subset\cup_iX^{-\omega} v_{i,g}$ and $\sum_{i,g}|X|^{-|v_{i,g}|}<\varepsilon$. Then
$A\subset\cup_{i,g}\mathscr{T}_{v_{i,g}}\cdot g$, and we have that
$\sum_{i,g}\mu_{(G,X^*)}(\mathscr{T}_{v_{i,g}})<\varepsilon\mu_{(G,X^*)}(\mathscr{T})$.
nodes.statement_short: Cover by cylinders and hence by small tiles.

nodes.name: Apply the tile inequality.
nodes.statement:
Then
$\mu_{(G,Y^*)}(\alpha(A))\leq\sum\mu_{(G,Y^*)}(\alpha(\mathscr{T}_{v_{i,g}}))\leq\sum\mu_{(G,X^*)}(\mathscr{T}_{v_{i,g}})<\varepsilon\mu_{(G,X^*)}(\mathscr{T})$.
Since $\varepsilon$ is arbitrary, we are done.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the tile inequality.

nodes.name: Reduce $\mu_Y\circ\alpha\le\mu_X$ to closed subsets of $\mat
nodes.statement:
We will now prove that $\mu_{(G,Y^*)}\circ\alpha\leq\mu_{(G,X^*)}$. Since both
$\mu_{(G,Y^*)}\circ\alpha$ and $\mu_{(G,X^*)}$ are invariant under multiplication by $g\in G$ it
suffices to prove this inequality for sets $A\subset\mathscr{T}$. Since any Borel $A$ is a union of a
closed set and a set of arbitrarily small measure, it suffices to prove the inequality for closed
sets, as $\mu_{(G,Y^*)}\circ\alpha$ is absolutely continuous with respect to $\mu_{(G,X^*)}$ by
above.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce $\mu_Y\circ\alpha\le\mu_X$ to closed subsets of $\mathscr{T}$.

nodes.name: Take closed $A$ and its level-$n$ tile hulls $A_n$.
nodes.statement:
So let $A\subset\mathscr{T}$ be a closed set. For each $n$, let $A_n$ be the union of all tiles
$\mathscr{T}_v,v\in X^n,$ that have non-empty intersection with $A$.
nodes.statement_short: Take closed $A$ and its level-$n$ tile hulls $A_n$.

nodes.name: Claim: $A=\cap_n A_n$.
nodes.statement:
Let us show that $A=\cap_n A_n$.
Suppose $x\in\cap A_n$, and $x$ is not in $A$. Then for each $n$ there is $v_n\in X^n$ such that
$\mathscr{T}_{v_n}$ has nonempty intersection with $A$ and $x\in\mathscr{T}_{v_n}$. It follows that $x$ has
some representation $u_nv_n\in X^{-\omega}$. Since the number of such representations is finite, we may
choose subsequence $n_k$ such that $v_{n_k}$ is the beginning of some word $v\in X^{-\omega}$. Since $A$ is
compact it follows that $A$ has nonempty intersection with $\cap_k\mathscr{T}_{v_{n_k}}$, thus
$\cap_k\mathscr{T}_{v_{n_k}}$ contains at least two points, which is impossible.
nodes.statement_short: Claim: $A=\cap_n A_n$.

nodes.name: Assume $x\in\cap A_n\setminus A$ and pick tiles $\mathscr{T}
nodes.statement:
Suppose $x\in\cap A_n$, and $x$ is not in $A$. Then for each $n$ there is $v_n\in X^n$ such that
$\mathscr{T}_{v_n}$ has nonempty intersection with $A$ and $x\in\mathscr{T}_{v_n}$.
nodes.statement_short: Assume $x\in\cap A_n\setminus A$ and pick tiles $\mathscr{T}_{v_n}$.

nodes.name: Pass to a subsequence of nested prefixes.
nodes.statement:
It follows that $x$ has
some representation $u_nv_n\in X^{-\omega}$. Since the number of such representations is finite, we may
choose subsequence $n_k$ such that $v_{n_k}$ is the beginning of some word $v\in X^{-\omega}$.
nodes.statement_short: Pass to a subsequence of nested prefixes.

nodes.name: Compactness gives two points in a shrinking intersection: im
nodes.statement:
Since $A$ is
compact it follows that $A$ has nonempty intersection with $\cap_k\mathscr{T}_{v_{n_k}}$, thus
$\cap_k\mathscr{T}_{v_{n_k}}$ contains at least two points, which is impossible.
nodes.statement_short: Compactness gives two points in a shrinking intersection: impossible.

nodes.name: Inequality for $A_n$, then limit for $A$.
nodes.statement:
Since $A_n$ is the union of some tiles of level $n$, which are disjoint up to sets of measure $0$,
the inequality also holds for all $A_n$. Going to the limit, we get the inequality for $A$.
nodes.statement_short: Inequality for $A_n$, then limit for $A$.

nodes.name: Symmetry gives equality.
nodes.statement: By interchanging $X$ and $Y$ we get the reverse inequality, and we are done.
nodes.statement_short: Symmetry gives equality.

nodes.name: Build the graph $\Gamma$ from the nucleus.
nodes.statement:
Construct the graph $\Gamma$ with the elements of $\mathcal{N}$ as vertices, for each edge labeled by
$(x,x)$ in $\mathcal{N}$ we have the edge in $\Gamma$ with the same starting and end vertices, and labeled
by $x$; and for each edge in $\mathcal{N}$ labeled by $(x,y)$ for $x\neq y$ there is an edge in $\Gamma$
with the same starting vertex that ends in the trivial element and labeled by $x$.
nodes.statement_short: Build the graph $\Gamma$ from the nucleus.

nodes.name: $\mathcal{U}=\mathcal{O}(\Gamma)$: $w\in\mathcal{U}$ iff $V_
nodes.statement:
Then the set
$\mathcal{U}$ coincides with the set $\mathcal{O}(\Gamma)$. Indeed, $h\in V_{\Gamma}(w)$ if and only if
there is a path in $\mathcal{N}$ labeled by $(w,w)$ that ends in $h$, thus $w\in\mathcal{U}$ if and only
if $V_{\Gamma}(w)=\{1\}$.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal{U}=\mathcal{O}(\Gamma)$: $w\in\mathcal{U}$ iff $V_\Gamma(w)=\{1\}$.

nodes.name: Every vertex reaches 1, so $\{1\}$ is the only terminal comp
nodes.statement:
For every nontrivial element $h\in\mathcal{N}$ there exists a word $v\in X^{*}$
such that $h(v)\neq v$. It follows that there exists a path in the graph $\Gamma$ from $h$ to $1$.
Hence the component $\{1\}$ is the only strongly connected component of the graph $\Gamma$ without
outgoing edges.
nodes.statement_short: Every vertex reaches 1, so $\{1\}$ is the only terminal component.

nodes.name: Corollary 4 gives measure number 1.
nodes.statement:
By Corollary~\ref{cor_meas_sum_meas} the measure number of $\Gamma$ is $1$, and
$\mathcal{U}=\mathcal{O}(\Gamma)$.
nodes.statement_short: Corollary 4 gives measure number 1.

nodes.name: First statement from Lemma 1.
nodes.statement:
The first statement of the lemma now follows from
Lemma~\ref{lemma_set V open dense}.
nodes.statement_short: First statement from Lemma 1.

nodes.name: Claim: $\mathcal{U}$ is closed under asymptotic equivalence.
nodes.statement:
Let us show that the set $\mathcal{U}$ is closed under the asymptotic equivalence relation (then
the set $\mathcal{U}\times G$ is also closed). It is sufficient to show that if there is a path in
$\mathcal{N}$ labeled by $(u,v)$ and $u\in\mathcal{U}$ ($v\in\mathcal{U}$) then $v\in\mathcal{U}$
($u\in\mathcal{U}$). Let the path in $\mathcal{N}$ labeled by $(u,v)$ end in $h$. It follows that $u$ is
asymptotically equivalent to $v\cdot h$. Suppose there is a path in $\mathcal{N}$ labeled by $(v,v)$ that
ends in $g$. It follows that $v$ is asymptotically equivalent to $v\cdot g$. Thus $u$ is
asymptotically equivalent to $v\cdot gh$ which is asymptotically equivalent to $u\cdot h^{-1}gh$.
By definition, there is a path in $\mathcal{N}$ labeled by $(u,u)$ which ends in $h^{-1}gh$. Since
$u\in\mathcal{U}$ we get $h^{-1}gh=1$, thus $g=1$.
nodes.statement_short: Claim: $\mathcal{U}$ is closed under asymptotic equivalence.

nodes.name: Reduce to paths labeled $(u,v)$.
nodes.statement:
It is sufficient to show that if there is a path in
$\mathcal{N}$ labeled by $(u,v)$ and $u\in\mathcal{U}$ ($v\in\mathcal{U}$) then $v\in\mathcal{U}$
($u\in\mathcal{U}$).
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to paths labeled $(u,v)$.

nodes.name: A path labeled $(u,v)$ ending in $h$ gives $u\sim v\cdot h$.
nodes.statement:
Let the path in $\mathcal{N}$ labeled by $(u,v)$ end in $h$. It follows that $u$ is
asymptotically equivalent to $v\cdot h$.
nodes.statement_short: A path labeled $(u,v)$ ending in $h$ gives $u\sim v\cdot h$.

nodes.name: A path labeled $(v,v)$ ending in $g$ gives $v\sim v\cdot g$.
nodes.statement:
Suppose there is a path in $\mathcal{N}$ labeled by $(v,v)$ that
ends in $g$. It follows that $v$ is asymptotically equivalent to $v\cdot g$.
nodes.statement_short: A path labeled $(v,v)$ ending in $g$ gives $v\sim v\cdot g$.

nodes.name: Conjugate to a $(u,u)$ path, forcing $g=1$.
nodes.statement:
Thus $u$ is
asymptotically equivalent to $v\cdot gh$ which is asymptotically equivalent to $u\cdot h^{-1}gh$.
By definition, there is a path in $\mathcal{N}$ labeled by $(u,u)$ which ends in $h^{-1}gh$. Since
$u\in\mathcal{U}$ we get $h^{-1}gh=1$, thus $g=1$.
nodes.statement_short: Conjugate to a $(u,u)$ path, forcing $g=1$.

nodes.name: Reduce to injectivity of $\pi$ on $\sigma^{-1}(w)$ for a.e.
nodes.statement:
Since every point of $\lims$ has at most $|X|$ preimages under $\mathsf{s}$, it is enough to show that for
almost every $w\in X^{-\omega}$ the map $\pi_{\lims[]}:\sigma^{-1}(w)\rightarrow\mathsf{s}^{-1}(\pi_{\lims[]}(w))$
is one-to-one.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to injectivity of $\pi$ on $\sigma^{-1}(w)$ for a.e. $w$.

nodes.name: Suppose $\pi(wx)=\pi(wy)$ with $x\ne y$.
nodes.statement:
Suppose that for some $w\in X^{-\omega}$ and $x\neq y$ in $X$ we have
$\pi_{\lims[]}(wx)=\pi_{\lims[]}(wy)$.
nodes.statement_short: Suppose $\pi(wx)=\pi(wy)$ with $x\ne y$.

nodes.name: Then the $(w,w)$-prefix path ends at a nontrivial element, s
nodes.statement:
It follows that $wx,wy$ are asymptotically equivalent, thus
there is a left-infinite path in $\mathcal{N}$ labeled by $(wx,wy)$. It follows that the prefix of this
path labeled by $(w,w)$ must end in the nontrivial element, so $w\not\in\mathcal{U}$.
nodes.statement_short: Then the $(w,w)$-prefix path ends at a nontrivial element, so $w\notin\mathcal{U}$.

nodes.name: $\mathcal{U}$ has full measure by Lemma 2.
nodes.statement:
Since
$\mu_u(\mathcal{U})=1$ by Lemma~\ref{lemma U_open_dense_meas1}, we are done.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal{U}$ has full measure by Lemma 2.

nodes.name: Surjective from a compact set: suffices to prove injectivity
nodes.statement:
By definition, the map $\rho|_{\mathscr{T}_u}:\mathscr{T}_u\rightarrow\mathsf{T}_u$ is surjective, and $\mathscr{T}_u$ is
compact. Hence in order to prove that $\rho$ is a homeomorphism it is left to show that $\rho$ is
injective on $\mathscr{T}_u$.
nodes.statement_short: Surjective from a compact set: suffices to prove injectivity.

nodes.name: Take representatives $wu$, $vu$
nodes.statement:
Take $x,y\in\mathscr{T}_u$, and let $wu\in X^{-\omega}$ represent $x$ and $vu\in X^{-\omega}$
represent $y$. Suppose that $\rho(x)=\rho(y)$. By Proposition~\ref{prop_asympt_Moore_diagr} it
means that there is a left-infinite path in $\mathcal{N}$ labeled by $(wu,vu)$. Since
$u\in\mathcal{U}^*$, this path must end in $1$. It follows, that $wu$ and $vu$ represent the same
point of the tile $\mathscr{T}_u$, and $x=y$.
nodes.statement_short: Take representatives $wu$, $vu$; equal images give a nucleus path ending in 1, so $x=y$.

nodes.name: Disjointness of translates of $\mathscr{T}_u$.
nodes.statement:
To prove the second claim, take $x\in\mathscr{T}_u\cdot g\cap\mathscr{T}_u\cdot g'$. Then $x$ is represented by
two asymptotically equivalent sequences $wu\cdot g$ and $w'u\cdot g'$. It follows that there is a
path in the nucleus $\mathcal{N}$ labeled by $(u,u)$ which ends in $g'g^{-1}$. Then $g=g'$ since
$u\in\mathcal{U}^*$.
nodes.statement_short: Disjointness of translates of $\mathscr{T}_u$.

nodes.name: Restrict to the images of $\mathcal{U}\times G$ and $\mathca
nodes.statement:
Consider the sets $\tilde{\limGs}=\pi_{\limGs[]}(\mathcal{U}\times G)$ and
$\tilde{\lims}=\pi_{\lims[]}(\mathcal{U})$. It follows that $\tilde{\limGs}/G=\tilde{\lims}$.
nodes.statement_short: Restrict to the images of $\mathcal{U}\times G$ and $\mathcal{U}$.

nodes.name: Complements are null by Lemma 2.
nodes.statement:
Since
the set $\mathcal{U}$ has measure $1$ by Lemma~\ref{lemma U_open_dense_meas1}, the complements of
$\mathcal{U}\times G$, of $\tilde{\limGs}$, and of $\tilde{\lims}$ have measure $0$.
nodes.statement_short: Complements are null by Lemma 2.

nodes.name: Properness is inherited
nodes.statement:
Since the group $G$ acts properly on $\limGs$, the same holds for $\tilde{\limGs}$. It is left to
prove the freeness.
nodes.statement_short: Properness is inherited; freeness remains.

nodes.name: A fixed point gives a $(u,u)$ nucleus path, so $g=1$.
nodes.statement:
Suppose $x\cdot g=x$ for $x\in\tilde{\limGs}$ and $g\in G$. Let $u\cdot h$ be a
representative of $x$ in $X^{-\omega}\times G$. It follows that $u\cdot hg$ is asymptotically equivalent
to $u\cdot h$, thus there is a path in $\mathcal{N}$ labeled by $(u,u)$ that ends in $h^{-1}gh$. Since
$u\in\mathcal{U}$ we have $g=1$.
nodes.statement_short: A fixed point gives a $(u,u)$ nucleus path, so $g=1$.

nodes.name: Hence a covering map.
nodes.statement:
Hence the projection $\tilde{\limGs}\rightarrow\tilde{\lims}$ is a covering map, and the statement
follows.
nodes.statement_short: Hence a covering map.

nodes.name: Use the full-measure sets of Theorem 17 and Proposition 16.
nodes.statement:
Consider the sets $\tilde{\lims}$ and $\tilde{\limGs}$ of full measure from the previous theorem.
For every $u\in\mathcal{U}^*$ we have $\mathsf{T}_u\subset\tilde{\lims}$, $\mathscr{T}_u\cdot
g\subset\tilde{\limGs}$ for every $g\in G$, and $\rho^{-1}(\mathsf{T}_u)=\bigsqcup_{g\in G} \mathscr{T}_u\cdot g$
by Proposition~\ref{x_j_homeo}.
nodes.statement_short: Use the full-measure sets of Theorem 17 and Proposition 16.

nodes.name: Suffices to compare on each $\mathsf{T}_u$.
nodes.statement:
Since $\tilde{\lims}=\cup_{u\in\mathcal{U}^*}\mathsf{T}_u$ by
Lemma~\ref{lemma U_open_dense_meas1} it suffices to show that for any $u\in\mathcal{U}^*$ the
restriction of $\mu_{*}$ on $\mathsf{T}_u$ is equal to the restriction of $\mathsf{m}$.
nodes.statement_short: Suffices to compare on each $\mathsf{T}_u$.

nodes.name: Take a Borel $A\subset\mathscr{T}_u$
nodes.statement:
Take a Borel set
$A\subset\mathscr{T}_u$ and consider its preimage $\pi^{-1}_{\limGs[]}(A)=\sqcup_{g\in\mathcal{N}} A_g\cdot g$.
Then $\pi^{-1}_{\lims[]}(\rho(A))=\sqcup_{g\in\mathcal{N}} A_g$. Here the union is disjoint because if
$w\in{A_g\cap{}A_h}$ then $w\cdot g$ and $w\cdot h$ are asymptotically equivalent to $vu$ and $v'u$
respectively, for some $v,v'\in X^{-\omega}$. It follows that $vu\cdot g^{-1}$ is equivalent to $v'u\cdot
h^{-1}$. Since $u\in\mathcal{U}$, $g=h$.
nodes.statement_short: Take a Borel $A\subset\mathscr{T}_u$; the preimage of its image is the disjoint union of the $A_g$.

nodes.name: Compute $\mathsf{m}(\rho(A))$.
nodes.statement:
Hence
\[
\mathsf{m}(\rho(A))=\mu_u(\pi^{-1}_{\lims[]}(\rho(A)))=\mu_u(\sqcup_{g\in\mathcal{N}}
A_g)=\sum_{g\in\mathcal{N}}\mu_u(A_g).
\]
nodes.statement_short: Compute $\mathsf{m}(\rho(A))$.

nodes.name: Quotient measure property gives equality.
nodes.statement:
By the property of the quotient measure
\[
\mu_{*}(\rho(A))=\mu(A)=\sum_{g\in\mathcal{N}}\mu_u(A_g)=\mathsf{m}(\rho(A)).
\]
nodes.statement_short: Quotient measure property gives equality.

nodes.name: Recall uniformly $d$-to-one endomorphisms
nodes.statement:
We will use notions and results from \cite{hoffman:Bernoulli}. First recall that a measure
preserving map with entropy $\log{d}$ is called {\it uniformly $d$-to-one endomorphism} if it is
almost everywhere $d$-to-one and the conditional expectation of each preimage is $1/d$.  The
standard example is $(X^{-\omega},\sigma,\mu_u)$, which is uniformly $|X|$-to-one.
nodes.statement_short: Recall uniformly $d$-to-one endomorphisms; the shift is the standard example.

nodes.name: Claim: $(\lims,\mathsf{s},\mathsf{m})$ is uniformly $|X|$-to
nodes.statement:
Next we want to show
that $(\lims,\mathsf{s},\mathsf{m})$ is also uniformly $|X|$-to-one. By
Proposition~\ref{prop_measure_prop_lims} the map $\pi:X^{-\omega}\rightarrow\lims$ is injective on the
preimages $\sigma^{-1}(w)$ for almost all $w\in X^{-\omega}$, that is, $\pi$ is {\it tree adapted} in
terminology of \cite{hoffman:Bernoulli}. We can apply Lemma~2.3 from \cite{hoffman:Bernoulli},
which says that a tree adapted factor of a uniform $d$-to-one endomorphism is again uniform
$d$-to-one endomorphism. In particular, the shift $\mathsf{s}$ is the map of maximal entropy $\log |X|$.
nodes.statement_short: Claim: $(\lims,\mathsf{s},\mathsf{m})$ is uniformly $|X|$-to-one.

nodes.name: Proposition 15 makes $\pi$ tree adapted.
nodes.statement:
By
Proposition~\ref{prop_measure_prop_lims} the map $\pi:X^{-\omega}\rightarrow\lims$ is injective on the
preimages $\sigma^{-1}(w)$ for almost all $w\in X^{-\omega}$, that is, $\pi$ is {\it tree adapted} in
terminology of \cite{hoffman:Bernoulli}.
nodes.statement_short: Proposition 15 makes $\pi$ tree adapted.

nodes.name: Hoffman-Rudolph Lemma 2.3: tree adapted factors stay uniform
nodes.statement:
We can apply Lemma~2.3 from \cite{hoffman:Bernoulli},
which says that a tree adapted factor of a uniform $d$-to-one endomorphism is again uniform
$d$-to-one endomorphism.
nodes.statement_short: Hoffman-Rudolph Lemma 2.3: tree adapted factors stay uniform.

nodes.name: Hence maximal entropy.
nodes.statement: In particular, the shift $\mathsf{s}$ is the map of maximal entropy $\log |X|$.
nodes.statement_short: Hence maximal entropy.

nodes.name: Quote Hoffman-Rudolph Theorem 5.5.
nodes.statement_short: Quote Hoffman-Rudolph Theorem 5.5.

nodes.name: Recall generating functions.
nodes.statement:
Recall the definition of tree very weak Bernoulli and generating function. Let $(Y,S,\mu)$ be
uniformly $d$-to-one and $f:Y\rightarrow{R}$ be a tree adapted function to a compact metric space
$R$ with metric $D$. The function $f$ is called \textit{generating} if the $\sigma$-algebra on $Y$
is generated by $S^{-i}f^{-1}(\mathcal{B}),i\geq{0}$, where $\mathcal{B}$ is the $\sigma$-algebra
of Borel sets of the space $R$.
nodes.statement_short: Recall generating functions.

nodes.name: Recall tree very weak Bernoulli via the tree distance $t_n$.
nodes.statement:
Informally, ``tree very weak Bernoulli'' means that for almost all pairs of points in $Y$ their
trees of preimages are close. To give a formal definition note that since $S$ is uniformly
$d$-to-one, for almost all points $y\in Y$ the set $S^{-k}(y)$ contains exactly $d^k$ points, i.e.
the tree of preimages is a $d$-regular rooted tree. The set $\{1,\ldots, d\}^{*}$ of finite words
over $\{1,\ldots,d\}$ can be considered as a $d$-regular rooted tree, where every word $v$ is
connected with $vx$ for $x\in\{1,\ldots,d\}$, and the root is the empty word $\emptyset$. We can
use the tree $\{1,\ldots, d\}^{*}$ to label the trees of preimages. For almost all points $y\in Y$
there is a map $T_y:\{1,\dots,d\}^*\rightarrow{Y}$ such that $T_y(\emptyset)=y$ and
$T_y(\sigma(v))=S(T_y(v))$ for all nonempty words $v\in \{1,\dots,d\}^*$. Every map $T_y$ is tree
adapted, and it is uniquely defined up to an automorphism of the tree $\{1,\dots,d\}^*$. Then
$(Y,S,\mu)$ and $f$ are called {\it tree very weak Bernoulli} if for any $\varepsilon>0$ and all
sufficiently large $n$ there is a set $W=W(\varepsilon,n)\subset Y$ with $\mu(W)>1-\varepsilon$
such that for any $y,y'\in{W}$
\begin{equation} t_n(y,y')=\min_\psi \frac{1}{n}\sum_{v\in \{1,\dots,d\}^{*}, |v|\leq
n}d^{-|v|}D(f(T_y(v)),f(T_{y'}(\psi(v))))<\varepsilon,
\end{equation}
where the minimum is taken over all automorphisms $\psi$ of the tree $\{1,\dots,d\}^*$. Notice that
the definition of $t_n$ does not depend on the choice of $T_y$.
nodes.statement_short: Recall tree very weak Bernoulli via the tree distance $t_n$.

nodes.name: Claim: the identity is a tree very weak Bernoulli generator.
nodes.statement:
Let us show that $(\lims,\mathsf{s},\mathsf{m})$ is tree very weak Bernoulli for the identity map
$id:\lims\rightarrow\lims$. It immediately follows that $id$ is tree adapted and generating. Take a
point $x\in\lims$ and let $x$ be represented by some $w\in X^{-\omega}$. Define the map
$T_x:X^{*}\rightarrow\lims$ by the rule $T_x(v)=\pi(wv)$. It is enough to show that $
t_n(x,x')\rightarrow 0, n\rightarrow\infty, $ for almost all $x,x'\in\lims$. Using
(\ref{eqn_diam_tile_goes_zero}) we can find $n_1$ such that $\max_{v\in
X^n}\rm{diam}(\mathsf{T}_v)<\epsilon/2$ for all $n\geq n_1$. It means that $D(\pi(wv),\pi(w'v))<\epsilon/2$
for all $v,|v|\geq n_1$ (here $D$ is a fixed metric on the limit space $\lims$). Thus, taking
$\psi$ to be the identical tree automorphism, we have that
\[
t_n(x,x')<\frac{n_1}{n} \rm{diam}(\lims)+\frac{n-n_1}{n}\frac{\epsilon}{2}<\frac{n_1}{n}
\rm{diam}(\lims)+\frac{\epsilon}{2}<\epsilon
\]
for $n>2n_1\rm{diam}(\lims)/\epsilon$. Hence $(\lims,\mathsf{s},\mathsf{m})$ and $id$ are tree very weak
Bernoulli, which finishes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Claim: the identity is a tree very weak Bernoulli generator.

nodes.name: Identity is generating
nodes.statement:
It immediately follows that $id$ is tree adapted and generating. Take a
point $x\in\lims$ and let $x$ be represented by some $w\in X^{-\omega}$. Define the map
$T_x:X^{*}\rightarrow\lims$ by the rule $T_x(v)=\pi(wv)$.
nodes.statement_short: Identity is generating; define $T_x(v)=\pi(wv)$.

nodes.name: Suffices: $t_n(x,x')\to0$ a.e.
nodes.statement:
It is enough to show that $
t_n(x,x')\rightarrow 0, n\rightarrow\infty, $ for almost all $x,x'\in\lims$.
nodes.statement_short: Suffices: $t_n(x,x')\to0$ a.e.

nodes.name: Shrinking tile diameters (3) bound distances.
nodes.statement:
Using
(\ref{eqn_diam_tile_goes_zero}) we can find $n_1$ such that $\max_{v\in
X^n}\rm{diam}(\mathsf{T}_v)<\epsilon/2$ for all $n\geq n_1$. It means that $D(\pi(wv),\pi(w'v))<\epsilon/2$
for all $v,|v|\geq n_1$ (here $D$ is a fixed metric on the limit space $\lims$).
nodes.statement_short: Shrinking tile diameters (3) bound distances.

nodes.name: Identity tree automorphism gives $t_n<\epsilon$.
nodes.statement:
Thus, taking
$\psi$ to be the identical tree automorphism, we have that
\[
t_n(x,x')<\frac{n_1}{n} \rm{diam}(\lims)+\frac{n-n_1}{n}\frac{\epsilon}{2}<\frac{n_1}{n}
\rm{diam}(\lims)+\frac{\epsilon}{2}<\epsilon
\]
for $n>2n_1\rm{diam}(\lims)/\epsilon$.
nodes.statement_short: Identity tree automorphism gives $t_n<\epsilon$.

nodes.name: Conclude tree very weak Bernoulli.
nodes.statement:
Hence $(\lims,\mathsf{s},\mathsf{m})$ and $id$ are tree very weak
Bernoulli, which finishes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude tree very weak Bernoulli.

nodes.name: Regular nonzero
nodes.statement:
The measure $\Phi_*\mu$ is a non-zero regular Borel measure on $L$. It is left to prove that it is
translation invariant.
nodes.statement_short: Regular nonzero; remains translation invariance.

nodes.name: $G$-invariance from equivariance.
nodes.statement:
Since the measure $\mu$ is $G$-invariant and the map $\Phi$ is
$G$-equivariant, the measure $\Phi_*\mu$ is $G$-invariant.
nodes.statement_short: $G$-invariance from equivariance.

nodes.name: Scaling under $\phi_L$ via the proof of Proposition 10.
nodes.statement:
By the property of the map $\Phi$ we
have $\phi_L(\Phi(A))=\Phi(\tau_{x_0}(A))g_0$ for every Borel set $A\subset\limGs$. Notice that
since the map $\phi$ is injective, we get $\mu(A)=|X|\mu(\tau_x(A))$ (see the proof of
Proposition~\ref{prop_measure lims propert}) and hence $\Phi_*\mu(B)=|X|\Phi_*\mu(\phi_L(B))$ for
every Borel set $B\subset L$.
nodes.statement_short: Scaling under $\phi_L$ via the proof of Proposition 10.

nodes.name: Invariance under the dense set $\cup_n\phi_L^n(G)$, hence un
nodes.statement:
It follows that the measure $\Phi_*\mu$ is $\cup_n
\phi_L^n(G)$-invariant. Since $\phi_L$ is contracting, the set $\cup_n \phi_L^n(G)$ is dense in the
Lie group $L$. Hence $\Phi_*\mu$ is $L$-invariant.
nodes.statement_short: Invariance under the dense set $\cup_n\phi_L^n(G)$, hence under $L$.

nodes.name: Haar uniqueness: $\Phi_*\mu=c\lambda$
nodes.statement:
The measure $\Phi_*\mu$ is the Haar measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$ by the above example. Since the Haar
measure is unique up to multiplicative constant, we have that $\Phi_*\mu=c\lambda$ for some
constant $c>0$ and we need to prove that $c=1$.
nodes.statement_short: Haar uniqueness: $\Phi_*\mu=c\lambda$; need $c=1$.

nodes.name: Recall integrality and multiplicity of the tile covering.
nodes.statement:
Recall that $\mu(\mathscr{T})$ is integer by Proposition~\ref{theor_tile_measure}, and almost every point
of $\limGs$ is covered by $\mu(\mathscr{T})$ tiles $\mathscr{T}\cdot g$ by Proposition~\ref{points_above}.
nodes.statement_short: Recall integrality and multiplicity of the tile covering.

nodes.name: Multiplicity transfers to $\mathbb{R}^n$ for both measures.
nodes.statement:
Hence $\Phi_*\mu(T)=\Phi_*\mu(\Phi(\mathscr{T}))=\mu(\mathscr{T})$ is integer and almost every point of
$\mathbb{R}^n$ is covered by $\mu(\mathscr{T})$ tiles $T+g$, $g\in\mathbb{Z}^n$, with respect to the measure
$\Phi_*\mu$, and thus with respect to the Lebesgue measure $\lambda$. It follows that, if
$\chi_{T+g}$ is the characteristic function of $T+g$, then $\sum_{g\in\mathbb{Z}^n}\chi_{T+g}=\mu(\mathscr{T})$
almost everywhere with respect to both measures.
nodes.statement_short: Multiplicity transfers to $\mathbb{R}^n$ for both measures.

nodes.name: Integrate over the unit cube to get $\lambda(T)=\mu(\mathscr
nodes.statement:
Hence
\[
\Phi_*\mu(T)=\mu(\mathscr{T})=\int_I\sum_{g\in\mathbb{Z}^n}\chi_{T+g}d\lambda=\sum_{g\in\mathbb{Z}^n}\int_{I+g}\chi_T
d\lambda=\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\chi_T d\lambda=\lambda(T),
\]
where $I$ is the unit cube in $\mathbb{R}^n$.
nodes.statement_short: Integrate over the unit cube to get $\lambda(T)=\mu(\mathscr{T})$.

nodes.name: Positivity gives $c=1$.
nodes.statement: Since $\mu(\mathscr{T})$ is positive, $c=1$.
nodes.statement_short: Positivity gives $c=1$.

nodes.name: Set up $\mathcal{M}$, the partial self-covering and the prei
nodes.statement:
Let $f$ be a sub-hyperbolic rational function and let $\mathcal{M}=\hat{\mathbb{C}}\setminus\overline{P}_f$, where $P_f$
is the post-critical set of $f$. Then $f$ defines a $d$-fold partial self-covering $f:
f^{-1}(\mathcal{M})\rightarrow\mathcal{M}$. Take a base point $t\in\mathcal{M}$ and let $T_t$ be the tree of preimages
$f^{-n}(t)$, $n\geq 0$, where every vertex $z\in f^{-n}(t)$ is connected by an edge to $f(z)\in
f^{-n+1}(t)$.
nodes.statement_short: Set up $\mathcal{M}$, the partial self-covering and the preimage tree.

nodes.name: Define the iterated monodromy group.
nodes.statement:
The fundamental group $\pi_1(\mathcal{M},t)$ acts by automorphisms on $T_t$ through the
monodromy action on every level $f^{-n}(t)$. The quotient of $\pi_1(\mathcal{M},t)$ by the kernel of its
action on $T_t$ is the \textit{iterated monodromy group} $IMG(f)$ of the map $f$.
nodes.statement_short: Define the iterated monodromy group.

nodes.name: Nekrashevych Thm 6.4.4: limit dynamical system of $IMG(f)$ i
nodes.statement:
The group
$IMG(f)$ is contracting self-similar group and the limit dynamical system $(\lims[IMG(f)],\mathsf{s})$ is
conjugated to $(J(f),f)$ by Theorem~6.4.4 in \cite{self_sim_groups}.
nodes.statement_short: Nekrashevych Thm 6.4.4: limit dynamical system of $IMG(f)$ is conjugate to $(J(f),f)$.

nodes.name: $\mathsf{m}$ goes to $\mu_f$
nodes.statement:
Under this conjugation the
measure $\mathsf{m}$ is send to the measure $\mu_f$, and we can apply
Theorem~\ref{theor_lims_conju_Bernoulli} to the dynamical system $(J(f),f,\mu_f)$.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathsf{m}$ goes to $\mu_f$; apply Theorem 19.
